note: Existing-source, strict-license-screened public gallery. Additional historical photos remain held from this site. Anatomy overlays are teaching annotations, not a separate verified voucher determination.

tiles.heading: 01 · ROOTED KNOTROOT AND EVEN FOXTAIL
tiles.details: Perennial rhizomatous grass with culms roughly 30–120 cm and a compact cylindrical panicle typically 3–8(10) cm (FNA). Inspect an attached rootstock before treating this as an annual foxtail. Existing source-labelled Croatian rhizome and habit photos teach the organs, but do not certify a Hays County voucher.
tiles.short: LOOK HERE FIRST: a short, hard, knotty perennial rhizome beneath a dense, nearly even-width foxtail head
tiles.status: GROWTH FORM TAUGHT — SAME-VOUCHER TEXAS PLANT NEEDED

tiles.heading: 02 · TRUE HAIR-FRINGE LIGULE
tiles.details: FNA reports the true ligule <1 mm; Kew/GrassBase reports about 0.4–1.2 mm. Leaf blades often 2–8 mm wide. The source-labelled sl16 photo shows collar placement but cannot establish a measured Texas ligule. Do not point to purple stigmas or sheath-mouth hairs as the ligule.
tiles.short: Open the inner blade–sheath junction; ligule is a short fringe of hairs, not an erect membrane
tiles.status: TRUE COLLAR SOURCE PHOTO — CALIBRATED LOCAL MACRO NEEDED

tiles.heading: 03 · COUNT BRISTLES BELOW A SPIKELET
tiles.details: At 10–20× trace bristles to the individual spikelet's short basal branch; count several mature units. FNA gives 4–12 and 2–12 mm, while the local Williamson County treatment commonly finds 6–7 (range 4–12), about 1.3–7.5 mm. Pink feathery stigmas are flower parts, NOT bristles. The archived sl24 macro shows shafts but not a Texas same-voucher attachment count.
tiles.short: Usually 4–12 persistent bristles, about 2–12 mm, BELOW each spikelet; these are sterile branchlets, not awns
tiles.status: ARCHIVED BRISTLE PHOTO — ATTACHMENT COUNT UNMEASURED

tiles.heading: 04 · OPEN BOTH GLUMES
tiles.details: FNA describes lower glume ~one-third and upper ~one-half to two-thirds of spikelet length; the local Texas treatment instead gives lower glume 1.1–1.5 mm and upper 1.7–1.8 mm on 2.2–2.5 mm spikelets. Published proportions differ: never enforce one ratio without a measured mature specimen. The source-labelled sl29 montage shows Glu' and Glu''; its original labels do not replace same-plant verification.
tiles.short: Mature spikelets ~2–2.8 mm; lower glume short and 3-veined, upper glume longer and commonly 5-veined

tiles.heading: 05 · TWO FLORETS, NO LEMMA AWNS
tiles.details: Lower sterile lemma approximately spikelet length and generally 5-veined; upper fertile lemma about 2–2.6 mm (Kew) with conspicuous transverse ridges. Open a ripe spikelet to see both lemmas and paleas separately. No true long lemma awn: the persistent basal bristles belong to sterile panicle branchlets. Do not invent fine arrows where the archived pixels cannot resolve an organ.
tiles.short: Lower sterile or staminate floret plus a hardened, transversely wrinkled upper fertile lemma
tiles.status: REAL LABELLED REPRODUCTIVE MONTAGE — CALIBRATED DISSECTION NEEDED

tiles.heading: 06 · CHECK THE LOCAL FOXTAIL LOOK-ALIKES
tiles.details: S. italica is an introduced annual with a heavy often lobed head and usually fewer bristles; S. reverchonii has a slender often interrupted head with sparse 2–8 mm bristles where present; S. scheelei often has one very long 10–35 mm projecting bristle. S. pumila and S. viridis are annual look-alikes, not installed canonical genus species. Use actual roots, attached mature spikelets and the true ligule; do not infer local nativity from Croatian images.
tiles.short: Perennial knotty rhizome and many bristles separate it from annual foxtails and the other native Setaria
tiles.status: FIELD COMPARISON — MATCHED TEXAS VOUCHERS NEEDED

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: KNOTROOT BRISTLEGRASS (Setaria parviflora): Start at the PERENNIAL BASE. The new real source photo shows short knotty rhizomes and buds, a reliable contrast with many annual foxtails. Next peel back an attached leaf to see the TRUE fringe-of-hairs ligule (about 0.4–1.2 mm in Kew). Examine a dense uniform foxtail panicle, then ONE spikelet with its 4–12 persistent bristles attached below it, NOT the purple feathery flowering stigmas. The new photographed 3-mm montage labels lower and upper GLUMES and LEMMAS; these are real botanical parts. Source collection is Croatia, and a matched Texas voucher remains pending.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: Start with the locally archived living plant and follow one entire slender foxtail head down to its leafy basal tuft. Then open the separate actual excavated knotty rhizome photo; it shows the connected hard underground stem and attached roots that the live field shot does NOT expose.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: FNA reports the true ligule <1 mm; Kew/GrassBase reports about 0.4–1.2 mm. Leaf blades often 2–8 mm wide. The source-labelled sl16 photo shows collar placement but cannot establish a measured Texas ligule. Do not point to purple stigmas or sheath-mouth hairs as the ligule.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: At 10–20× trace bristles to the individual spikelet's short basal branch; count several mature units. FNA gives 4–12 and 2–12 mm, while the local Williamson County treatment commonly finds 6–7 (range 4–12), about 1.3–7.5 mm. Pink feathery stigmas are flower parts, NOT bristles. The archived sl24 macro shows shafts but not a Texas same-voucher attachment count.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: Distinguish from annual yellow foxtail S. pumila and green foxtail S. viridis using actual knotty perennial rhizomes; neither is a canonical species here. S. reverchonii has longer interrupted heads with bristles much sparser, S. scheelei has usually one very long conspicuous projecting bristle and longer loose/tapered head. Foxtail millet S. italica is cultivated/escaped annual; its dense head alone is insufficient.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

Next peel back an attached leaf to see the TRUE fringe-of-hairs ligule (about 0.4–1.2 mm in Kew). Examine a dense uniform foxtail panicle, then ONE spikelet with its 4–12 persistent bristles attached below it, NOT the purple feathery flowering stigmas. The new photographed 3-mm montage labels lower and upper GLUMES and LEMMAS; these are real botanical parts. Source collection is Croatia, and a matched Texas voucher remains pending.
memory_rule: RHIZOME first: short hard KNOTTY perennial base → tiny HAIR ligule → dense evenly cylindrical bristly head → separate persistent BRISTLES from magenta STIGMAS → Glu/Lem under a ruler.
safety_note: Five exact-species public-safe images physically archived (one sl26 spikelet, sl13 rhizome, sl16 ligule, sl24 bristle macro, sl29 glume-lemma montage). 2 new macro JPEGs independently read back and source licenses CC BY-SA 4.0 verified 2026-10-24. Two new gross markers target actual visible bristle SHAFT and purple stigma in sl24, not an invisible bristle insertion. Croatian photos do NOT certify Hays identity; same-voucher mature count and mobile QA missing. 2026-10-26: source CC BY-SA 4.0 whole-plant image sl1 is now a locally archived EXIF-free JPEG, with three gross-only arrow markers; original NC-licensed S. scheelei comparison remains preserved with attribution, subject to noncommercial use and individual license recheck. Site must pass rights-filtered deployment before live claim.
field_rule: Avoid native/introduced calls or true species ID solely from bristle silhouette. Count several attached mature spikelets and study rootstock on the same plant.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
